claims.summary: Federal law preempts state laws that eliminate flexibility to decide whether and to what extent to pay interest or other compensation on funds placed in escrow accounts or assess fees for such accounts.

claims.quote: The OCC agrees and has amended its final preemption determination accordingly. claims.summary: A State interest-on-escrow law does not need to completely remove all flexibility to be preempted.

claims.summary: The OCC has incorporated the interest-on-escrow laws in Guam and the U.S. Virgin Islands into its preemption determination.

claims.quote: The OCC has removed it from the final regulatory text.

claims.quote: The OCC is issuing this final preemption determination, which concludes that (1) the National Bank Act preempts section 5-601 of New York's General Obligations Law, the State's interest-on-escrow law; (2) thirteen other States have laws with substantively equivalent terms; and (3) these substantively equivalent State laws are also preempted.

claims.quote: Section 5-601 of New York's General Obligations Law requires ``mortgage investing institutions'' to pay ``dividends or interest at a rate of not less than two per centum per year . . . or a rate prescribed by the [New York] superintendent of financial services'' on escrow account balances.
claims.summary: Mortgage investing institutions must pay dividends or interest at a rate of not less than two per centum per year or a rate prescribed by the New York superintendent of financial services on escrow account balances.

claims.quote: This statutory obligation applies whenever the institution ``maintains an escrow account pursuant to any agreement executed in connection with a mortgage on any one to six family residence occupied by the owner or on any property owned by a cooperative apartment corporation'' located in New York.
claims.summary: The statutory obligation applies when the institution maintains an escrow account pursuant to any agreement executed in connection with a mortgage on any one to six family residence occupied by the owner or on any property owned by a cooperative apartment corporation located in New York.

claims.quote: This New York law also requires the institution to credit the interest to the escrow account on a quarterly basis, and it generally prohibits the assessment of a service charge in connection with maintaining an escrow account.
claims.summary: The institution must credit the interest to the escrow account on a quarterly basis and generally prohibit the assessment of a service charge in connection with maintaining an escrow account.

claims.quote: courts addressing preemption questions in this context must do as Barnett Bank did and likewise take account of those prior decisions of this Court and similar precedents.

claims.quote: Finding that the State law limitations would interfere with this flexibility, which was critical to the Federal scheme, the Fidelity Court concluded that the State law was preempted.

claims.summary: Courts must determine if state laws interfere with national banks' ability to exercise federal powers effectively and efficiently and conclude accordingly.

claims.summary: A state law addressing the transfer and devolution of property in the state, as a generally applicable infrastructure law, is typically not preempted.

claims.quote: national banks are subject to general State laws in their ``dealings and contracts,'' unless those laws expressly conflict with Federal law, frustrate the purpose of national banks, or impair their ability to efficiently exercise their Federally authorized powers.
claims.summary: National banks are subject to general state laws in their dealings and contracts unless those laws expressly conflict with federal law, frustrate the purpose of national banks, or impair their ability to efficiently exercise their federally authorized powers.

claims.quote: the McClellan Court held that the State law was not preempted.
claims.summary: A state law that is generally applicable and does not impose greater conditions or restrictions on national banks than on other citizens is not preempted.

claims.summary: A state tax law is not preempted if national banks are generally subject to state laws on contracts, the acquisition and transfer of property, and the right to collect and be sued for debts.

a State law prevents or significantly interferes with a Federal power when it interferes with critical flexibility granted to a national bank under Federal law, interferes with a national bank's effectiveness or efficiency in exercising its Federal power, or qualifies a Federal power in an unusual way.

claims.summary: Paragraphs (c)(1) introductory text and (c)(1)(i) apply to returns filed for taxable years ending on or after May 20, 2026. Paragraph (c)(2) applies to returns filed on or after November 30, 2020. Paragraph (d)(3) applies to transfers that occur on or after November 30, 2020.

claims.quote: This document sets forth these final rules related to certain provisions of the No Surprises Act regarding the Federal independent dispute resolution (IDR) process, which was established as part of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2021 (CAA). These rules finalize new requirements relating to the disclosure of information that group health plans and health insurance issuers offering group or individual health insurance coverage must include along with the initial payment or notice of denial of payment for certain items and services subject to the surprise billing protections in the No Surprises Act.
claims.affected_party: group health plans and health insurance issuers offering group or individual health insurance coverage
claims.summary: Final rules finalize new requirements for disclosure of information with initial payment or notice of denial of payment for certain items and services subject to the surprise billing protections in the No Surprises Act.

claims.quote: These final rules also require plans and issuers to communicate information by using claim adjustment reason codes (CARCs) and remittance advice remark codes (RARCs), as specified in guidance, when providing any paper or electronic remittance advice (ERA) to an entity that does not have a contractual relationship with the plan or issuer.
claims.summary: Final rules require plans and issu,ers to communicate information using CARCs and RARCs when providing remittance advice to entities without a contractual relationship.

claims.quote: This document also finalizes amendments to certain requirements related to the open negotiation period preceding the Federal IDR process, the initiation of the Federal IDR process, the Federal IDR dispute eligibility review process, and the payment and collection of administrative fees and certified IDR entity fees.
claims.summary: Final rules amend requirements related to the open negotiation period, initiation of the Federal IDR process, dispute eligibility review process, and payment and collection of fees.

claims.quote: This document also finalizes the definition of bundled payment arrangements, amends requirements related to batched items and services and amends the rules for extensions of timeframes due to extenuating circumstances.
claims.summary: Final rules finalize the definition of bundled payment arrangements, amend requirements related to batched items and services, and amend rules for extensions of timeframes due to extenuating circumstances.

claims.quote: Additionally, this document finalizes provisions that require plans and issuers to register in the Federal IDR portal.
claims.summary: Final rules require plans and issuers to register in the Federal IDR portal.

claims.quote: each FEHB Program contract must require a carrier to comply with requirements described in sections 9816 and 9817 of the Code, sections 716 and 717 of ERISA, and sections 2799A-1 and 2799A-2 of the PHS Act (as applicable) in the same manner as these provisions apply for a group health plan or health insurance issuer offering group or individual health insurance coverage.
claims.summary: Carriers must comply with specific requirements from sections 9816, 9817, 716, 717, 2799A-1, and 2799A-2 of the Code, ERISA, and PHS Act in the same manner as they apply to group health plans or health insurance issuers.

claims.quote: plans and issuers and nonparticipating providers and facilities may utilize to resolve certain disputes regarding out-of-network rates under section 9816 of the Code, section 716 of ERISA, and section 2799A-1 of the PHS Act.
claims.affected_party: plans and issuers, nonparticipating providers and facilities
claims.summary: Plans and issuers, along with nonparticipating providers and facilities, may utilize the Federal IDR process to resolve disputes regarding out-of-network rates under specified sections.

claims.quote: plans and issuers and nonparticipating providers of air ambulance services to utilize the Federal IDR process.
claims.affected_party: plans and issuers, nonparticipating providers of air ambulance services
claims.summary: Plans and issuers, along with nonparticipating providers of air ambulance services, may utilize the Federal IDR process.

claims.quote: prohibitions on balance billing for certain items and services and requirements related to disclosures about balance billing protections.
claims.affected_party: health care providers, facilities, providers of air ambulance services
claims.summary: Health care providers, facilities, and providers of air ambulance services must comply with prohibitions on balance billing for certain items and services and requirements related to disclosures about balance billing protections.
